strategies.name: Faber 10-month trend filter
strategies.rationale: Price-vs-200-day (~10-month) trend, the canonical Faber (2007) GTAA regime filter. A broad US equity index spends most of its time in persistent bull regimes punctuated by a few sustained bear markets; staying invested above the long MA and flat below harvests the equity risk premium while sidestepping the largest drawdowns (2000-02, 2008, 2020). Edge is drawdown control and volatility reduction, not pure timing alpha, so risk-adjusted return improves modestly over buy-and-hold.

strategies.name: Golden/Death cross regime with crisis convexity
strategies.rationale: 50/200 crossover is the most widely watched equity regime signal; the death cross tends to fire before the worst of sustained bear markets. Traded long-short, the short leg is a tail hedge that pays in 2008/2020 rather than an alpha engine. Shorting fights the equity premium during whipsaw bull corrections, so raw Sharpe is honestly a notch below the long-only version, but the crisis convexity is genuine and diversifying.

strategies.name: Intermediate trend workhorse 20/100
strategies.rationale: A ~1-month vs ~5-month crossover sits at the trend horizon where equity-index autocorrelation is empirically strongest and stable. Faster than the Faber filter so it re-enters uptrends sooner after corrections, slower than daily noise so turnover and whipsaw stay contained at 1bp costs. A robust middle-of-the-road trend workhorse.

strategies.name: 12-month time-series momentum
strategies.rationale: Trailing 12-month return sign is the Moskowitz-Ooi-Pedersen TSMOM signal, one of the most out-of-sample-validated anomalies across asset classes and decades. On a US equity index it captures persistent drift and regime persistence; long-only avoids the drag of shorting a positive-drift asset while keeping the protective exit in prolonged downtrends.

strategies.name: 6-month momentum
strategies.rationale: Six-month trailing return balances momentum persistence against the lag of the 12-month signal, historically a sweet spot in the intermediate-horizon momentum literature. Reacts faster to regime turns than 252d while still filtering short-term noise. Diversifies the trend book across horizon.

strategies.name: Vol-targeted 12-month momentum
strategies.rationale: 12-month momentum sign scaled by inverse realized volatility. Equity volatility clusters and is negatively correlated with returns, so inverse-vol scaling automatically trims exposure into turbulent, drawdown-prone regimes and levers up in calm trends. Vol targeting historically lifts momentum Sharpe by roughly 10-20% and stabilizes the risk profile. My highest-conviction construction.

strategies.name: Fast vol-targeted momentum, long-short
strategies.rationale: Shorter 6-month signal with a responsive 20-day vol estimate, traded long-short. The short leg plus inverse-vol scaling concentrates exposure exactly when it should be cut, producing crisis-alpha convexity. Faster signal means more whipsaw and the short side drags in choppy bulls, so honest expected Sharpe is moderate, but it diversifies the slower trend signals.

strategies.name: Donchian 100-day breakout
strategies.rationale: Classic Turtle-style channel breakout: go long on a new 100-day high. New highs on an equity index signal regime continuation and fresh trend legs; long-only skips the whipsaw-prone downside breaks that fight the equity premium. A price-native trend entry that is uncorrelated in timing with the MA and return-based signals.

strategies.name: Slow Donchian 200-day breakout
strategies.rationale: A very-long-horizon 200-day channel acts as a coarse regime filter: participate only when the index makes genuinely new long-term highs. Few trades, low turnover, robust to noise, and captures the fat right tail of secular bull runs. The slow cousin of the 100-day breakout, trading responsiveness for durability.

strategies.name: 3-month momentum
strategies.rationale: Quarter-long trailing return captures shorter-term trend persistence and post-earnings/news drift, re-entering quickly after shallow pullbacks. Honestly the thinnest of the set: higher turnover and more whipsaw make it the most cost- and noise-sensitive, so I hold modest conviction, but it usefully diversifies horizon at the fast end of the trend spectrum.

strategies.name: RSI2 deep-oversold dip buy (long-only)
strategies.rationale: Connors RSI-2 buy-the-dip. Sharp 2-day drops in a broad index are dominated by liquidity-demanding sellers (de-risking, margin calls, stop cascades); providing liquidity into that panic earns the short-horizon reversal / overreaction premium. Post-2000 S&P daily return autocorrelation is negative, giving this structural support. Long-only because the index's upward drift makes fading strength a chronic loser. This is my highest-conviction mean-reversion signal.

strategies.name: RSI2 moderate-oversold dip buy (long-only)
strategies.rationale: Same liquidity-provision mechanism as the deep RSI-2 buy, but a higher entry threshold fires on the more frequent shallow dips. Smaller edge per trade, but far more observations means better statistical robustness and less reliance on a handful of crisis days. Long-only to avoid drift drag.

strategies.name: RSI3 oversold bounce (long-only)
strategies.rationale: A 3-period oscillator smooths single-day noise relative to RSI-2, reducing one-day whipsaw while still capturing 2-3 day overreaction. Same index short-term-reversal logic; distinct entry dynamics give diversification against the pure 2-day variants.

strategies.name: RSI5 symmetric fade (long/short)
strategies.rationale: Fades both oversold and overbought extremes over roughly a week to harvest reversion symmetrically. The short-the-strength leg captures genuine short-term overextension but surrenders the equity drift, so I expect a materially lower Sharpe than the long-only variants. Included as an honest test of two-sided reversion, not as a top pick.

strategies.name: Bollinger 20/2 lower-band buy (long-only)
strategies.rationale: Canonical band touch. A close below the 20-day, 2-sigma lower band is a volatility-normalized ~2-sigma dislocation from the monthly mean, which historically mean-reverts on indices. The volatility scaling adapts the threshold to regime, unlike a fixed percentage drop. Long-only harvests the bounce without paying drift on shorts.

strategies.name: Bollinger 10/1.5 fast-band buy (long-only)
strategies.rationale: A tighter, faster band trades the frequent shallow intraweek dislocations rather than rare extremes. Higher turnover and smaller per-trade edge, but many more trades. Same volatility-normalized oversold-bounce logic on a shorter memory.

strategies.name: Bollinger 15/2.5 extreme-touch fade (long/short)
strategies.rationale: Only wide ~2.5-sigma touches trigger, isolating rarer, higher-conviction dislocations on both sides. The two-sided design tests whether extreme overbought touches also revert; the short leg gives up drift, capping the Sharpe. A selective, low-frequency reversion play.

strategies.name: Bollinger 50/2 correction dip buy (long-only)
strategies.rationale: A ~2-month lookback flags dislocations from the longer mean, catching deeper, more persistent oversold conditions (shallow corrections) rather than daily noise. Captures the multi-week oversold-bounce as institutional rebalancing and buy-the-dip flows restore the index. Long-only.

strategies.name: 3-day short-term reversal (long/short)
strategies.rationale: Direct implementation of the classic short-term reversal factor (Lehmann 1990; Lo-MacKinlay 1990): buy 3-day losers, sell 3-day winners on overreaction. A 3-day window materially lowers turnover versus a 1-day reversal while retaining the signal, so it survives realistic costs better. The always-in short leg drags Sharpe but keeps constant exposure to the reversal premium.

strategies.name: 5-day weekly reversal (long/short)
strategies.rationale: Weekly-horizon reversal: overreaction accumulated over five sessions tends to unwind. Lower turnover than the 1-3 day versions makes it the most cost-robust reversal variant here, at the cost of a weaker raw signal. Honest, tradeable, and diversifying against the oscillator-based dip buys.

strategies.name: Vol-managed 12M momentum (fast vol)
strategies.rationale: Canonical time-series momentum (Moskowitz-Ooi-Pedersen 2012): the sign of the trailing ~12-month return is the most robust single trend signal across assets and decades. Sizing inversely to 20-day realized vol implements the Moreira-Muir (2017) / Barroso-Santa-Clara (2015) volatility-management result: high-vol states cluster in bear markets and carry low forward return, so de-risking into rising vol raises Sharpe and sharply cuts the momentum-crash left tail. A 20-day vol window reacts fast enough to trim exposure entering turmoil. Long-only, so it holds cash rather than shorting the equity risk premium. Highest-conviction line.

strategies.name: Vol-managed 12M momentum (stable vol)
strategies.rationale: Same 12-month trend sign, but a 60-day vol estimator is far less jumpy than a 20-day one, so position size drifts smoothly and turnover (hence transaction cost and whipsaw) falls materially. The trade-off is slower de-risking at the very onset of a crash. Held alongside the fast-vol version because the true optimal vol horizon is unknown and averaging the two diversifies estimation error.

strategies.name: Vol-managed 6M momentum
strategies.rationale: A 6-month lookback recognizes regime shifts sooner than the 12-month rule, exiting downtrends earlier, while inverse-vol scaling still controls momentum-crash risk. The cost is more whipsaw in choppy ranges. Intermediate horizon diversifies the 252-day signals; genuine but slightly lower conviction than the 12-month core.

strategies.name: Vol-managed 3M momentum
strategies.rationale: Short-horizon trend for the fastest defensive exits, vol-scaled to suppress the added noise. A 3-month signal is largely noise on an index and turns over frequently, so net-of-cost edge is thin; included mainly as a fast-reacting complement to the slower momentum sleeves, and honest expectation is modest.

strategies.name: Golden-cross defensive filter (50/200)
strategies.rationale: The 50/200-day cross is the most-watched equity regime filter: long above, cash below. It captures the persistence of multi-month bull/bear regimes and has historically sidestepped the worst of 2000-02 and 2008. Edge is genuine trend persistence plus a degree of self-reinforcement from how widely it is followed. Very low turnover, so costs are negligible; value is chiefly drawdown reduction rather than higher raw return.

strategies.name: Faber 200-day timing
strategies.rationale: Approximates Faber's (2007) price-versus-200-day (10-month) rule, with fast=2 standing in for spot price. One of the most out-of-sample-robust timing rules known, working across asset classes and long histories with minimal parameters. Primary contribution is truncating deep drawdowns; expected return is close to buy-and-hold but realized risk is much lower, lifting Sharpe.

strategies.name: Absolute time-series momentum 12M
strategies.rationale: Textbook TSMOM: long when the trailing year is positive, short when negative. On a single up-drifting equity index the short leg is a structural drag and gets whipsawed by bear-market rallies, so I do NOT expect a higher Sharpe than the long-only versions. Stand behind it as a crisis-alpha / low-correlation diversifier that pays off in protracted declines, not a stand-alone Sharpe maximizer — an honest tail hedge, priced as such.

strategies.name: Absolute momentum 6M defensive
strategies.rationale: A 6-month absolute-momentum gate to cash: simpler than the vol-managed sleeve and quicker than the 12-month rule at leaving downtrends. It forgoes vol scaling, so it keeps the full momentum-crash risk on entry/exit turns, but the raw trend filter itself is robust. A clean, low-parameter defensive rule at an intermediate horizon.

strategies.name: Donchian 1-year breakout
strategies.rationale: Turtle-style channel breakout: a new 1-year high confirms an uptrend, a new 1-year low a downtrend. The long window filters short-term noise and captures durable trends. On an equity index the short side underperforms because of the upward drift and sharp V-shaped recoveries off lows, so honest net Sharpe is modest; kept for trend-capture diversification and distinct entry logic versus the moving-average rules.

strategies.name: Intermediate cross (20/100)
strategies.rationale: A faster trend filter than 50/200: it enters and exits regimes earlier and tracks intermediate swings, at the cost of more whipsaws in sideways markets. Run to diversify the horizon of the defensive-timing sleeve — decorrelating the entry/exit timing from the slow 200-day rules reduces the chance that a single unlucky crossover point drives results.

strategies.name: Golden Cross Trend Filter (50/200)
strategies.rationale: The classic 50/200-day SMA crossover captures the well-documented persistence of equity index trends and, crucially, sidesteps sustained bear markets (2000-02, 2008, 2022) by moving to cash. Long-only respects the equity risk premium: it participates in the drift while cutting left-tail exposure. Turnover is very low, so transaction costs are negligible. Its edge is risk reduction (lower drawdown/vol) more than excess return, which modestly lifts Sharpe over buy-and-hold.

strategies.name: Fast Dual-MA Whipsaw Probe (10/60)
strategies.rationale: An exploratory faster crossover that also goes short on downtrends. Faster MAs react sooner to reversals but generate frequent whipsaws in choppy, range-bound indices, and the short leg actively bets against the upward drift. Included as a lower-conviction point an automated search would sample: it tests whether quicker trend detection pays enough to offset whipsaw and negative-carry shorting. I expect it to underperform the slow long-only filter.

strategies.name: 12-Month Time-Series Momentum
strategies.rationale: Time-series momentum (Moskowitz-Ooi-Pedersen): a positive trailing ~12-month return predicts continued positive returns, an effect robust across asset classes and decades driven by underreaction to news and slow-moving capital. At ~250 trading days the signal is slow and stable, keeping turnover and costs low. Long-only to harvest the drift while stepping aside during protracted downtrends.

strategies.name: 2-Month Momentum Both-Sides Probe
strategies.rationale: A shorter ~2-month horizon straddling the zone where slower momentum fades into short-term reversal, run long-short. This is a deliberately uncertain sample: 40 days is fast enough to catch intermediate swings but noisy, and the short leg fights index drift. It probes whether an automated search finds edge in the intermediate horizon; I hold low conviction and expect it well below the slow long-only version.

strategies.name: Vol-Managed 6-Month Momentum
strategies.rationale: Combines the strongest two levers available: a ~6-month momentum sign scaled by inverse realized volatility. Moreira-Muir show vol-managed equity exposure raises Sharpe because volatility spikes (crises) are not compensated by proportionally higher returns, so de-risking when the 20-day vol is high avoids the worst crash clusters while momentum keeps direction correct. Long-only to compound the risk premium. My highest-conviction strategy in this set.

strategies.name: Slow Vol-Scaled Trend Both-Sides
strategies.rationale: A slower 12-month momentum sign with a smoother 60-day vol estimate, run long-short. The long vol-scaling still helps risk-adjusted return, but a slow 60-day vol window de-risks sluggishly into fast crashes, and the short leg concedes drift. An exploratory blend of the vol-target and long-short axes; decent but honestly capped below the responsive long-only variant.

strategies.name: 3-Day Short-Term Reversal
strategies.rationale: Broad equity indices exhibit robust short-horizon mean reversion: 1-5 day moves partly reverse as liquidity providers demand compensation for absorbing order-flow imbalances and overreaction corrects. Fading the trailing 3-day move (short after up, long after down) exploits this. Gross Sharpe is high, but daily turnover is heavy, so I discount substantially for transaction costs and slippage. Net edge survives but is materially reduced.

strategies.name: Connors RSI(2) Dip-Buy
strategies.rationale: A 2-period RSI is an extreme short-term oversold/overbought oscillator; RSI(2)<10 flags a sharp multi-day flush that, in an upward-drifting index, tends to snap back (the Connors mean-reversion system). Long-only: I buy deep oversold dips and avoid shorting overbought strength, which in an uptrending index is where naive RSI systems bleed. Real but partly backtest-mined, so I keep the expectation modest and cost-aware.

strategies.name: 20-Day Bollinger Mean-Reversion Dip-Buy
strategies.rationale: Standard 20-day, 2-sigma Bollinger bands: price piercing the lower band marks a statistically stretched short-term selloff that mean-reverts toward the moving average, the same daily reversal effect from a volatility-normalized angle (bands widen in high vol, demanding a larger move to trigger). Long-only avoids fighting the drift by shorting upper-band touches during trends. Correlated with the RSI dip-buy, so diversification benefit is limited.

strategies.name: 100-Day Donchian Breakout
strategies.rationale: A 100-day Donchian channel is slow trend-following: going long on new ~5-month highs rides established uptrends and, because indices spend most of their history near highs, keeps the position long through the drift while the short-of-new-lows exit pulls out during sustained declines. Long-only to avoid whipsaw shorts. Conceptually close to the momentum/MA rules (a trend family member), with edge from crash avoidance more than timing precision.
